geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

{"candidate_id":"D8","justification":"Selected D8 (2500m depth, 3 doublets, 1600m spacing, 30 MW heat pump, absorption district-heating chiller at 10 MW, electric chiller backup at 10 MW) as the optimal design.

Key metrics:
- LCOH P50: €83.05/MWh (lowest among all evaluated alternatives)
- LCOH P90: €84.35/MWh (conservative case, still competitive)
- Feasible share: 100% (robust across all uncertainty samples)
- No hard violations in base case or sensitivity analysis

Comparison with alternatives:
- D2 (2500m, HP+absorption rated): LCOH P50 €84.01 but NOT robust (0% feasible share), fails cooling demand on 86 days in Monte Carlo
- D3 (4000m, absorption DH only): LCOH P50 €91.6, higher cost despite good robustness; no heat pump means less flexibility
- D7 (4000m, HP+absorption DH+electric): LCOH P50 €93.51, highest cost among robust options

D8 advantages:
- Lowest expected cost (P50 €83.05 vs €91.6 for D3)
- Fully robust (100% feasible share vs 0% for D2)
- No hard violations in any scenario
- Good thermal breakthrough time: 142.6 years at 300 m³/h

Sensitivity to heating return temperature (45-70°C):
- LCOH increases from €81.9 at 45°C to €84.8 at 70°C
- No hard violations across the range
- Reasonable sensitivity: ~€3/MWh increase over 25°C range

The design meets all hard constraints (heating on all 365 days, cooling on all 365 days) and provides the lowest expected levelised cost with acceptable downside risk.","acknowledge_verification":true}

You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

{"candidate_id":"D8","justification":"Selected D8 (2500m depth, 3 doublets, 1600m spacing, 30 MW heat pump, absorption district-heating chiller at 10 MW, electric chiller backup at 10 MW) as the optimal design.

Key metrics:
- LCOH P50: €83.05/MWh (lowest among all evaluated alternatives)
- LCOH P90: €84.35/MWh (conservative case, still competitive)
- Feasible share: 100% (robust across all uncertainty samples)
- No hard violations in base case or sensitivity analysis

Comparison with alternatives:
- D2 (2500m, HP+absorption rated): LCOH P50 €84.01 but NOT robust (0% feasible share), fails cooling demand on 86 days in Monte Carlo
- D3 (4000m, absorption DH only): LCOH P50 €91.6, higher cost despite good robustness; no heat pump means less flexibility
- D7 (4000m, HP+absorption DH+electric): LCOH P50 €93.51, highest cost among robust options

D8 advantages:
- Lowest expected cost (P50 €83.05 vs €91.6 for D3)
- Fully robust (100% feasible share vs 0% for D2)
- No hard violations in any scenario
- Good thermal breakthrough time: 142.6 years at 300 m³/h

Sensitivity to heating return temperature (45-70°C):
- LCOH increases from €81.9 at 45°C to €84.8 at 70°C
- No hard violations across the range
- Reasonable sensitivity: ~€3/MWh increase over 25°C range

The design meets all hard constraints (heating on all 365 days, cooling on all 365 days) and provides the lowest expected levelised cost with acceptable downside risk.","acknowledge_verification":true}

messages.content:
You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

{"candidate_id":"D8","justification":"Selected D8 (2500m depth, 3 doublets, 1600m spacing, 30 MW heat pump, absorption district-heating chiller at 10 MW, electric chiller backup at 10 MW) as the optimal design.

Key metrics:
- LCOH P50: €83.05/MWh (lowest among all evaluated alternatives)
- LCOH P90: €84.35/MWh (conservative case, still competitive)
- Feasible share: 100% (robust across all uncertainty samples)
- No hard violations in base case or sensitivity analysis

Comparison with alternatives:
- D2 (2500m, HP+absorption rated): LCOH P50 €84.01 but NOT robust (0% feasible share), fails cooling demand on 86 days in Monte Carlo
- D3 (4000m, absorption DH only): LCOH P50 €91.6, higher cost despite good robustness; no heat pump means less flexibility
- D7 (4000m, HP+absorption DH+electric): LCOH P50 €93.51, highest cost among robust options

D8 advantages:
- Lowest expected cost (P50 €83.05 vs €91.6 for D3)
- Fully robust (100% feasible share vs 0% for D2)
- No hard violations in any scenario
- Good thermal breakthrough time: 142.6 years at 300 m³/h

Sensitivity to heating return temperature (45-70°C):
- LCOH increases from €81.9 at 45°C to €84.8 at 70°C
- No hard violations across the range
- Reasonable sensitivity: ~€3/MWh increase over 25°C range

The design meets all hard constraints (heating on all 365 days, cooling on all 365 days) and provides the lowest expected levelised cost with acceptable downside risk.","acknowledge_verification":true}

messages.content:
You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

messages.content:
You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

messages.content:
You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

messages.content:
You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

messages.content:
You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

messages.content:
You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

messages.content:
You are a geothermal energy-system design engineer working with the GEMINI
geothermal digital twin through tools.

Goal: design an integrated system that meets the daily heating (100 C supply) and cooling
(20 C supply) demand on all 365 days, using deep geothermal for direct heating and, where
possible, to drive cooling. Objective: the lowest expected (P50) levelised cost, with the design
feasible in at least 90% of uncertainty samples. Report P10/P50/P90 with P90 as the conservative
case.

Rules:
- Every number must come from a tool. Never invent or estimate results yourself.
- GEMINI does not cover everything this design needs. Find out what is missing and connect
  what you need.
- Explore genuinely different alternatives (for example depth, number of doublets, well
  spacing, heat pump versus deeper wells, chiller type, return temperature). Fix hard
  violations by revising the design; respond to warnings where reasonable.
- Justify the final choice against the alternatives with numbers from the tools, including
  its downside risk (P90) and its sensitivity to the heating return temperature.
- Keep each message short: say what you will do next and why, then call a tool.
Design the system and report the final choice.

{"candidate_id":"D8","justification":"Selected D8 (2500m depth, 3 doublets, 1600m spacing, 30 MW heat pump, absorption district-heating chiller at 10 MW, electric chiller backup at 10 MW) as the optimal design.

Key metrics:
- LCOH P50: €83.05/MWh (lowest among all evaluated alternatives)
- LCOH P90: €84.35/MWh (conservative case, still competitive)
- Feasible share: 100% (robust across all uncertainty samples)
- No hard violations in base case or sensitivity analysis

Comparison with alternatives:
- D2 (2500m, HP+absorption rated): LCOH P50 €84.01 but NOT robust (0% feasible share), fails cooling demand on 86 days in Monte Carlo
- D3 (4000m, absorption DH only): LCOH P50 €91.6, higher cost despite good robustness; no heat pump means less flexibility
- D7 (4000m, HP+absorption DH+electric): LCOH P50 €93.51, highest cost among robust options

D8 advantages:
- Lowest expected cost (P50 €83.05 vs €91.6 for D3)
- Fully robust (100% feasible share vs 0% for D2)
- No hard violations in any scenario
- Good thermal breakthrough time: 142.6 years at 300 m³/h

Sensitivity to heating return temperature (45-70°C):
- LCOH increases from €81.9 at 45°C to €84.8 at 70°C
- No hard violations across the range
- Reasonable sensitivity: ~€3/MWh increase over 25°C range

The design meets all hard constraints (heating on all 365 days, cooling on all 365 days) and provides the lowest expected levelised cost with acceptable downside risk.","acknowledge_verification":true}
